messages:
luke: Quick sync after the PM: trend we saw is config tweak -> slow drift -> late detection. We need faster detection and frequent mini-drills to validate rollback paths.

celine: Agreed. Proposal: biweekly 20m canary drills against a staging slice, plus a weekly "near-miss" summary email that surfaces short spikes that narrowly missed thresholds.

rachel: For the drills, can we codify a minimal checklist? e.g. create canary build, set traffic to 1%, validate health, induce a small error, verify auto-rollback triggers, confirm monitoring dashboards.

luke: Draft checklist idea: 1) create canary flag in FF service, 2) run synthetic job to raise error_rate by ~2.5x for 5m, 3) observe alerting and controller decisions, 4) rollback and validate recovery.

tom: On auto-rollback safety: we should require two signals before an irreversible rollback for production-canaries: error-rate spike AND latency increase OR CPU spike. Single noisy metric should only pause the rollout.

celine: Agreed. That will reduce false positives. We'll also limit max blast radius to 2% unless an owner overrides with extra checks.

rachel: Who owns implementing the coordinator logic that evaluates multi-signal rules? I can pick this up as a sprint task if owners are okay.

luke: Assign to rachel for the evaluation coordinator. Target branch and initial tests by 2026-04-08.

rachel: Will open a ticket INF-5001 and a draft PR with unit tests + a small integration harness.

devops-bot: Ops reminder: scheduled canary drill on 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC. Add participants with /remind.

tom: Telemetry gaps: we saw slow alerting downstream because our aggregation windows are 5m. For short drifts we should add a 1m fast-path for canaries that computes exponential moving avg to detect quick deviations.

celine: I'll add a telemetry ticket INF-5002: 1m aggregation + near-miss dashboard panel. Also add a histogram of per-minute false-trigger rate for last 30d so we can pick thresholds.

luke: Action items:
- rachel: build multi-signal coordinator (INF-5001), due 2026-04-08.
- celine: telemetry changes + near-miss dashboards (INF-5002), due 2026-04-07.
- tom: update rollout policy docs and feature-flag schema to include max_blast_pct and signal_rules, due 2026-04-06.
- luke: runbook update + schedule first drill (OPS-5002), due 2026-04-10.

rachel: I'll include an opt-in debug flag to force rollbacks in tests so we can validate the end-to-end path without impacting real traffic.

tom: Docs snippet idea for FF schema: ```
feature_flag: {
  "max_blast_pct": "2",
  "initial_pct": "0.5",
  "signal_rules": ["error_rate & latency", "cpu & error_rate"]
}
```

celine: Small ask: include a telemetry-backed guard that prevents expanding beyond 2% unless a follow-up approval workflow happens (UI + API). I'll sketch the flow.

luke: Plan to review progress in the ops sync next Monday 09:00. If blockers surface, tag #eng-oncall and DM owners.

devops-bot: Note: postmortem followup checklist added to OPS-5002.

rachel: PR opened INF-5001: https://git.redwood.ai/r/inf/multi-signal-coordinator (WIP). Adding reviewers.

luke: Great. Goal is to reduce detection->rollback median to <15m for critical regressions and have documented drills so playbooks are live and tested. :thumbsup:
